headline: Google Launches Gemini App for Windows with Alt + Space desktop AI assistance
summary: The new native app brings shortcut-based AI assistance to Windows 10 and 11 desktops, allowing users to summon Gemini with Alt + Space for drafting, summarizing, and content creation. It integrates with Google services like Gmail and Drive.
details: Google has launched a native Gemini app for Windows 10 and 11, bringing shortcut-based AI assistance directly to desktops. Users can summon the AI with a simple Alt + Space shortcut for tasks like drafting, document summaries, brainstorming, and content creation without needing a browser.

Announced on September 10, 2026, this launch marks the beginning of Gemini's native desktop capabilities on Windows. Google positions the app as a lightweight experience that runs in the background, providing assistance while users work in other applications.

The app is designed to reduce friction between tasks and AI prompts, allowing team members to access Gemini directly from their desktop workflows. It connects to Google services, enabling users to draft project summaries using information from Gmail and Google Drive.

Google also states that users can create images or videos from the desktop, citing Nano Banana and Gemini Omni in its launch materials. The company describes this Windows release as the initial phase of its native desktop experience, with more capabilities planned for the future.

For businesses, the app makes Gemini more accessible for teams already relying on Gmail and Drive, streamlining workflows that involve repetitive reading, context assembly, or drafting. It offers a convenience for generating first versions of documents.

While the app provides workflow convenience, businesses should start with repeatable, low-risk tasks where output can be easily checked by an employee. Google has confirmed global availability for Windows 10 and 11, but the initial materials do not specify new pricing or detailed business deployment options.

Further guidance on downloading the Windows app, using Alt + Space, and accessing its core functions is available in Google's September 11, 2026 Workspace update and Gemini Apps Help documentation. Future feature expansion is expected to clarify the experience across platforms and for different types of organizations.
